faqs.q: Do state differences affect my take-home pay?

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult ordinary-time earnings are higher in New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory, while Tasmania and South Australia tend to be lower. bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Full Time Minimum Wage Australia

If you are paid by the hour or considering a salary offer, knowing how to convert your hourly rate to an annual figure is essential. The **full time minimum wage australia** is a key benchmark, but your actual pay may differ depending on your award, industry, and state. This guide explains the conversion formula, the difference between minimum wage and award rates, casual loading, superannuation, and tax, with a focus on state differences in ordinary-time earnings.

## How to Convert Hourly to Annual Pay

The standard formula for annual gross pay is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, this becomes:

**Hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, if your hourly rate is $30, your annual gross pay is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It is a starting point for budgeting and comparing offers.

If you are paid fortnightly, your gross pay is simply the weekly amount multiplied by 2. For the minimum wage, that is $1004.90 × 2 = $2009.80 per fortnight before tax and super.

Use [the timesheet](/) to enter your base hourly rate. If you are a casual employee, tick the casual loading checkbox to add 25% on top. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The **full time minimum wage australia** is set by the Fair Work Commission and applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. From 1 July 2026, the rate is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour.

However, most employees are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or occupation. For example, a retail employee may have a higher base rate than the national minimum. Award rates also include penalty rates for weekends, public holidays, and overtime. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award.

If you are not covered by an award, the National Minimum Wage is your floor. Always check your award or agreement to ensure you are being paid correctly.

## Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. This loading is included in the casual minimum wage of $33.05 per hour. When using [the timesheet](/), tick the casual loading box to add this automatically.

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary earnings (not including overtime or casual loading in some cases). For the minimum wage, the employer must contribute an additional 12% of your ordinary time earnings to your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay; it is paid separately. The maximum contribution base for super is $270,830 per year, so super stops once your earnings exceed that amount.

## Tax on Your Annual Salary

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy. The tax-free threshold is $18,200. Income above that is taxed at:

- 15% from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted in this estimate.

For a full-time minimum wage earner ($52,254.80 per year), the tax would be approximately $5,092 plus Medicare, leaving a take-home pay of around $46,000. Use [reference tables](/data) for more detailed tax calculations.

## State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary-time employees. The national average as of May 2026 is $2083.70 per week. However, this is an average, not a median, and it varies by state. For example, the Australian Capital Territory and New South Wales typically have higher average earnings, while Tasmania and South Australia are lower. These differences reflect the mix of industries and occupations in each state, not a different minimum wage.

If you are comparing a salary offer across states, remember that the **full time minimum wage australia** is the same everywhere. But average earnings in your industry may be higher or lower depending on local demand. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page provides more context, but always check your specific award or agreement.

## Using the Timesheet for Your Calculations

The [timesheet](/) is the home page of this site. Enter your base hourly rate, select your hours per week (the default is 38), and tick casual loading if applicable. The tool will show your annual gross, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, super, and take-home pay. It uses the formula above and the latest tax and super rates.

Remember: this is an estimate. Your actual pay may differ due to unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, salary sacrifice, or specific award conditions. Always consult the Fair Work Ombudsman or a qualified professional for a binding determination.

## Summary

Converting your hourly rate to annual pay is straightforward: multiply by hours per week and 52. The **full time minimum wage australia** is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, but most workers are covered by higher award rates. Casual loading adds 25%, and super is paid on top. Tax and Medicare reduce your take-home pay. State differences in average earnings exist, but the minimum wage is uniform. Use [the timesheet](/) to calculate your own figures and [pay guides](/blog) to check your award.
